requirement: No fabricated or inflated social proof
pass_condition: No fabricated or inflated social proof anywhere : reviews, ratings, testimonials, client logos, ‘used by’ counts : and every rating in schema matches what’s visible on the page. (applies to product reviews, G2/Capterra badges, testimonials, follower/customer counts alike.)
fail_condition: AggregateRating 5.0/119 in schema while real counts are 1-6; a '3120 reviews' site header with no basis.
solution_pattern: P0 : remove fabricated review/rating schema before anything else; fabricated structured data risks a manual action and is the opposite of trust.

requirement: Genuine + hard-to-fake third-party proof shown
pass_condition: Only genuine proof is shown, plus hard-to-fake third-party proof fit to the model. (local/DTC: Google Business, Trustpilot; SaaS/B2B: G2, Capterra, analyst mentions, named clients; publisher: independent test data; services: verifiable case studies.)
fail_condition: Relying only on self-hosted testimonials you fully control.
solution_pattern: Third-party proof is harder to fake and more trusted than on-site claims : add it.

requirement: Real org identity (About / Our Story)
pass_condition: Clear ‘who runs this’: real org identity : About/Our-Story, team, mission, and ownership/funding transparency where it matters.
fail_condition: Anonymous brand with no team, story, or accountable owner.
solution_pattern: A verifiable human/organisation behind the site is a core trust signal.

requirement: Verifiable real-world footprint (NAP / legal entity)
pass_condition: Verifiable real-world footprint fit to the model. (local: address, phone, hours, consistent NAP; online-only: registered legal entity, real support channels, physical or corporate address.)
fail_condition: No address/phone, or a NAP that differs across the site and directories.
solution_pattern: Contactability and a real entity behind the site.

requirement: Complete, visible policies for the model
pass_condition: Policies complete and visible for your model. (ecom: shipping/returns/privacy; SaaS: terms, SLA, DPA, security; publisher/affiliate: disclaimers + affiliate/sponsorship disclosure; everywhere: privacy.)
fail_condition: Missing disclosure on affiliate/sponsored content; buried or absent returns/privacy.
solution_pattern: Policies are a baseline trust (and often legal) requirement.

requirement: Trust / compliance badges legitimate and unbroken
pass_condition: Trust/compliance badges are legitimate and unbroken. (accreditation e.g. BBB; security/compliance e.g. SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI; payment trust. A broken badge is a sitewide negative signal.)
fail_condition: A broken or expired badge (a sitewide negative signal), or a badge you're not entitled to.
solution_pattern: Every badge must be real and current.

requirement: Sourcing, methodology & corrections policy
pass_condition: Clear sourcing / methodology, and a visible corrections / last-updated policy.
fail_condition: Unsourced claims and no visible way to see when/if content is corrected.
solution_pattern: Show your work so the reader (and Google) can trust it.

requirement: Real named human byline (never Admin / CMS username / brand-only)
pass_condition: Real named human byline on content : never ‘Admin’, a CMS username, or brand-only. (the right author varies: founder/practitioner, named engineer/PM/DevRel, staff journalist/analyst, licensed professional, or researcher.)
fail_condition: 'Admin', a CMS username (e.g. tayyab910629), or brand-only bylines : signals negative expertise.
solution_pattern: Every content page needs an accountable, named human author.

requirement: Author's background genuinely matches the content's topic
pass_condition: The author’s stated background genuinely fits this piece’s topic, not just the business in general. (a generalist byline on a specialist topic reads as thin even with a real name attached : match the author to the piece, not just to the site.)
fail_condition: A real, credentialed author writing outside their actual area of experience : technically satisfies 'has an author' while adding no real expertise signal.
solution_pattern: Match the author to the topic, not just the byline to the page.

requirement: Dedicated author page (+ team directory)
pass_condition: Dedicated author page: name, photo, role, credentials/experience, first-hand background, links to their work : plus an author directory for teams.
fail_condition: A byline with no page, or a stub with no credentials/experience.
solution_pattern: The byline must resolve to real background about the author.

requirement: Byline links to a working author page
pass_condition: The byline links to that author page and the link actually works (not empty / dead).
fail_condition: Empty / dead author links (a very common CMS bug).
solution_pattern: A byline that links nowhere is worse than none.

requirement: Person schema + sameAs to real off-site profiles
pass_condition: Person schema + sameAs → the author’s real off-site profiles for the field. (LinkedIn broadly; GitHub for engineers; ORCID/Google Scholar for researchers; bar/license registries for law/finance/health; professional bodies.)
fail_condition: Person schema pointing to nothing, or to profiles that are inconsistent or don't exist.
solution_pattern: sameAs is how Google resolves the author as one known entity.

requirement: Author is a recognised entity off-site
pass_condition: Author is a recognised entity off-site: consistent profiles, guest bylines, talks/podcasts/conferences, quotes in trade media, dev/community or scholarly activity : identical name/role/bio everywhere.
fail_condition: Author exists only on your own site; inconsistent bios across the web.
solution_pattern: Authoritativeness of the author is corroborated off-domain.

requirement: Named experts over brand voice; keep author pages live
pass_condition: Named subject-matter experts preferred over a generic brand voice; author pages kept live after people leave; at scale, an editorial/author-governance system (bylines, review workflow, credential capture).
fail_condition: Deleting author pages when contributors leave; brand-only voice on expert topics.
solution_pattern: Preserve the entity association over time.

requirement: AI-assisted content reviewed & signed off by a named human
pass_condition: No fake / AI-generated authors; any AI-assisted content is reviewed and signed off by a named, accountable human.
fail_condition: AI-generated bylines with no human behind them; undisclosed AI.
solution_pattern: A named, accountable human must own AI-assisted content.

requirement: Author's writing style stays consistent across their own byline
pass_condition: Writing style stays recognisably consistent under one byline over time. (a rough check against uncredited ghostwriting or AI swaps : voice drift under an established name is often the only visible tell.)
fail_condition: Swapping in ghostwriters or AI output under an established author's name without disclosure : style drift is often the only visible tell.
solution_pattern: Inconsistent voice under one name is a quiet trust leak even when every other box is checked.

requirement: No fabricated or exaggerated credentials
pass_condition: No fabricated or exaggerated credentials in the bio or the schema.
fail_condition: Encoding invented degrees/licences in bios or schema.
solution_pattern: Credentials must be real and verifiable.

requirement: First-hand experience shown in a model-native form
pass_condition: Content shows genuine first-hand experience in a form native to the model. (original benchmarks/screenshots for tech/SaaS; project or before-after media for trades/DTC; first-party data/methodology for publishers/research; real client outcomes/case studies for B2B/agency.)
fail_condition: Generic, rewritten-from-the-internet content any site could publish.
solution_pattern: Experience is the human quality that verifies expertise : surface it.

requirement: Proof of doing the work is visible
pass_condition: Proof of doing the work is visible, not just claimed: data, artifacts, media, a ‘how we test / how we know’ methodology page.
fail_condition: Claiming expertise with zero demonstrable proof.
solution_pattern: Show, don't just claim, experience.

requirement: Expertise woven in + a single author box
pass_condition: Expertise woven into the topic sections + a single author box : not a bolted-on ‘from the founder’ section that breaks the heading flow.
fail_condition: Double-counting authorship (bio section AND author box); a person/voice heading breaking the outline.
solution_pattern: Declare authorship once; let the body READ expert.

requirement: Don't write outside real experience for traffic
pass_condition: Not publishing on topics with no real experience just for traffic : or if unavoidable, back it with a credentialed reviewer + primary sources.
fail_condition: Chasing a niche with no expertise purely for traffic.
solution_pattern: Enter a topic to add real value, not for search volume alone.

requirement: Credentialed reviewer on YMYL / regulated content
pass_condition: YMYL / regulated content carries a credentialed reviewer matched to the field. (health: MD/RD/pharmacist; finance: CFP/CPA/CFA; legal: licensed attorney; engineering/trades: PE/licensed pro.) “Reviewed by [Name, credential]” + reviewer page.
fail_condition: Health / safety / financial claims with no qualified reviewer.
solution_pattern: P0 for YMYL : a credentialed reviewer is the single biggest trust unlock.

requirement: Reviewer page + Person schema
pass_condition: Reviewer page + Person schema (credentials, license #, sameAs).
fail_condition: A 'reviewed by' line with no verifiable reviewer behind it.
solution_pattern: The reviewer must be a resolvable, credentialed entity.

requirement: Two-author model where the doer isn't credentialed
pass_condition: Two-author model where the doer isn’t formally credentialed: experienced author + credentialed reviewer.
fail_condition: Relying on an experienced-but-uncredentialed author alone on medical/financial claims.
solution_pattern: Experience + credential together clear the YMYL bar.

requirement: Authoritative, field-appropriate sources cited
pass_condition: Authoritative, field-appropriate sources cited. (regulators, standards bodies, peer-reviewed research, official documentation, primary data : not just your own claims.)
fail_condition: Citing nothing, or only yourself, on YMYL claims.
solution_pattern: Cite gold-standard sources on consequential claims.

requirement: Don't over-engineer non-YMYL pages
pass_condition: For non-YMYL topics, a formal reviewer is optional : depth, accuracy and first-hand experience carry it. Don’t over-engineer low-stakes pages.
fail_condition: Bolting a 'medically reviewed' block onto a fun, low-stakes post.
solution_pattern: Match the trust investment to the stakes.

requirement: Earn brand/author mentions from respected outlets
pass_condition: Brand + author mentions/links earned from respected outlets in your field. (trade press & industry analysts; local press for local; dev communities for tech; academic/citation for research.)
fail_condition: Assuming on-site claims of authority are enough.
solution_pattern: Authority is earned off-domain; PR is the strongest lever.

requirement: Structured-entity foundation (Wikidata)
pass_condition: Structured-entity foundation: Wikidata for brand/author; Wikipedia only if genuinely notable; knowledge-panel groundwork.
fail_condition: Creating a Wikipedia page without genuine notability (it gets removed).
solution_pattern: Give Google structured facts to build an entity / knowledge panel.

requirement: Cited in authoritative references
pass_condition: Cited in authoritative references for the model: round-ups, comparison/analyst sites, ‘best’ lists, expert or scholarly references.
fail_condition: No presence in the references your audience already trusts.
solution_pattern: Third-party citations corroborate authority.

requirement: Consistent identity across the web
pass_condition: Consistent identity across the web (NAP for local; org name / handles / sameAs for online-only).
fail_condition: Divergent names/addresses/bios across profiles and directories.
solution_pattern: Consistency lets Google merge you into one entity.

requirement: No bought or spammy links / paid reviews
pass_condition: No bought or spammy links, paid reviews, or private blog networks.
fail_condition: Purchasing links or reviews to fake authority.
solution_pattern: Never buy the signals : it's the opposite of the trust you're building.

requirement: Passes Who / How / Why
pass_condition: Passes Who / How / Why: named author (Who), AI/automation disclosed when used (How), made primarily to help people (Why).
fail_condition: Content made primarily to rank; undisclosed automation.
solution_pattern: People-first intent is the foundation E-E-A-T sits on.

requirement: First-hand expertise + depth; the goal is achieved
pass_condition: Demonstrates first-hand expertise + depth; the reader leaves having achieved their goal and had a satisfying experience.
fail_condition: Thin content that ranks but leaves the reader unsatisfied.
solution_pattern: Satisfy the searcher's actual goal, not just the keyword.

requirement: Clear purpose; real added value; scale care not just volume
pass_condition: Clear site purpose/focus; adds real value beyond what’s already out there; sources cited. If you scale content, scale the care, not just the volume.
fail_condition: Manufacturer-copy product pages; keyword-doorway 'docs'; undisclosed affiliate reviews.
solution_pattern: If you scale content, scale the CARE, not just the volume.

requirement: Clear purpose; real added value; scale care not just volume
pass_condition: Model-specific value in place. (ecom: unique product content, not manufacturer copy; SaaS: docs that solve the task, not keyword pages; affiliate/publisher: independent testing + clear affiliate disclosure.)
fail_condition: Manufacturer-copy product pages; keyword-doorway 'docs'; undisclosed affiliate reviews.
solution_pattern: If you scale content, scale the CARE, not just the volume.

requirement: Avoid search-engine-first / scaled patterns
pass_condition: Not mass-producing across many topics, or using extensive automation to churn content, hoping some ranks.
fail_condition: Faking dateModified; templating hundreds of near-duplicate pages.
solution_pattern: Avoid the exact patterns Google names as search-engine-first.

requirement: Avoid search-engine-first / scaled patterns
pass_condition: Not merely summarising others without added value; not chasing trends outside your expertise; not changing dates to fake freshness; not scaling thin templated pages.
fail_condition: Faking dateModified; templating hundreds of near-duplicate pages.
solution_pattern: Avoid the exact patterns Google names as search-engine-first.

requirement: Article/BlogPosting with author = Person
pass_condition: Article/BlogPosting with author = Person.
fail_condition: author as a string/Organization only, or absent.
solution_pattern: Tie every article to a Person author.

requirement: Person schema for author AND reviewer, each with sameAs
pass_condition: Person schema for the author AND the reviewer, each with sameAs.
fail_condition: Reviewer named on the page but missing from schema.
solution_pattern: The reviewer is an entity too, not just on-page text.

requirement: Model-appropriate schema, truthful only
pass_condition: Model-appropriate schema, truthful only. (ecom: Product + Review/AggregateRating from real data; SaaS: SoftwareApplication; local: Organization + LocalBusiness; HowTo/FAQPage where genuinely supported.)
fail_condition: Fabricated Review/Rating; schema that mismatches the visible page.
solution_pattern: Only mark up what's genuinely on the page.

requirement: Accurate datePublished + dateModified
pass_condition: Accurate datePublished + dateModified (never faked).
fail_condition: Bumping dateModified to fake freshness.
solution_pattern: Dates must be truthful.

requirement: about / mentions tie content to topic + brand entity
pass_condition: about / mentions tie the content to the topic + the brand entity.
fail_condition: No entity linking; orphaned content.
solution_pattern: Reinforce the entity graph.
